#138800. Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1356 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1356 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry.
  • The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions.
  • Over the past year, the organization has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry. The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga.

The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content.

Over the past year, the organization has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”.

Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience.

Sources indicate that its latest microdrama premiered in Los Angeles last week. The series, called “Inevitable,” stars Aki Avni, an Israeli film and television star who has been visible in American TV highlights for years (he had a stint on Fox’s 9/11-era thriller “24” years ago) but is now trying something largely unheard of in modern Hollywood: licensing his face to Shortical for the sake of its AI content.

According to recent reports, the project, which is wholly AI, used Avni’s face to create a digital avatar of him. In “Inevitable,” he plays himself – in a very meta plot in which he — the actor Aki Avni — licenses his face to a film studio, after which thriller-like antics ensue.

This is Shortical’s first foray into such a licensing deal, but it likely won’t be their last.

Recent findings suggest that in a phone interview, Avni told TechCrunch that he found the project both nerveracking and exciting. “Look, it’s a newly introduced era for artists,” the actor said. “AI is a new kind of art. It’s a new format. It’s always great to be the pioneer in something.”.

Guy Shimoni, the CEO of Shortical, emphasized the creative potential of the new tool. “One of the things that AI does is it enables smaller teams to be able to produce these movie-scale productions,” Shimoni remarked. “When we were doing mobile-first live action, we were limited by budget, but now we can serve them with epic fantasies. We have kingdoms and dragons. We have superheroes. We have werewolves.”.

But AI-generated romances involving werewolves — who, exactly, is watching this kind of thing?

Industry observers note that apparently, a lot of people. While China boasts the biggest microdrama audience globally, Shimoni indicates that most of his platform’s viewers are actually in the U.S. The industry’s viewer demographic skews heavily female. Many viewers may watch them to wind down at night, getting minor dopamine hits as they drift off to sleep. Many of the AI-generated programs that already exist on the organization’s website appear to have millions of views.

Now, Shortical is betting on the creation of a new generation of creators — those who, like Avni, are willing to surrender their likenesses for compensation. “LICENSE YOUR FACE” Shortical’s website advertises, explaining that interested parties can submit their social media handles to the company, which will then decide whether to offer them “a contract setting out the terms” of using their persona in the company’s AI-generated content.

A manufacturer rep told TechCrunch that this “offering is still in its early days and hasn’t yet resulted in any signed contracts.” They added: “The series with Aki is the first time Shortical has used a real person’s likeness, and it was done through a direct agreement with him rather than through the platform. Shortical hopes the series will draw more attention to face licensing and aims to promote the offering more actively following this launch.”.

Much of this trend has already taken hold in China where the microdrama industry originated, where AI-generated content is big, and where face-licensing is already a trend. Although the trend may not be a particularly profitable one for creators. A recent report in Rest of World found that Microdrama firms were paying people “between US$15 to US$700 to license their facial likenesses.”.

How much money is Shortical offering for its face-licensing deals? The tech giant isn’t saying. As for if Shortical will offer royalty-based compensation for creators — like the residual system in television, “It’s a case by case [basis],” Shimoni answers vaguely.

A Shortical representative further explained to TechCrunch that the company didn’t want to “share a specific figure” for Avni’s particular contract. However, the person said, he came “on as a partner in the project, and his compensation was in line with industry standards for a comparable non-AI acting role.”.

Sources indicate that for other actors, however, the deals may be quite different. Plus, many creatives are understandably unsettled by signs of automation creeping into their industry. Until recently, microdramas seemed like a safe, entry-level gateway into the entertainment industry, where young actors could gain experience on sets and hone their craft. Now, companies are downsizing and producing content that doesn’t even require real actors.

Jennifer Cooper, a longtime fan of the industry and founder of the consultancy firm Vertical Drama Love, notes that there’s a lot of distrust of AI — both from audiences and within the microdrama industry itself.

Industry observers note that “Everyone’s been impacted by AI,” she noted. “A lot of us have either lost work to AI or can see that it’s devastated this industry — [taking microdramas] from something that was a rare thing in the world, that was in growth, and providing work, particularly for young people…[and now] you know, it’s been decimated.”.

Questions of consent with AI likenesses have also dogged the industry (some creators claim they have had their likenesses stolen), which is something that Shortical is obviously trying to address with its newly introduced face-licensing endeavor.

Yet these licensing deals could also help to gig-ify the industry, creating a scenario in which creators team up with a distributor for the chance to platform their content (or their face), then receive payouts based on the audience engagement they’re allowed to generate. Shortical recently partnered with a company called Payouts.com, which describes itself as a “payout infrastructure platform powering creator and gig economy disbursements at scale.” The blueprint is to create a system by which creatives can seamlessly interact with Shortical’s platform and get paid.

In a recent development, cooper believes the push towards AI in the industry is driven by broader financial trends. Most of the microdrama business is led by startups, and VCs love to hear a growth game strategy involving automation. “For anyone to get investment at the moment in microdramas, they’ve got to mention the word AI,” she notes. “It’s like AI equals gold in everyone’s eyes.”.

Despite all the investment in this space, Cooper seems skeptical that there is actually a huge audience for this kind of content. “Some of it does get views. A lot of it doesn’t,” she remarked, of the AI content. “I think it’s being pushed on an audience more than there is an audience demand or wish for it.”.

Industry News: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Union's enlargement drive has regained momentum: Montenegro could become the bloc's 28th member in 2028, while Albania is rapidly advancing through accession talks and could complete accession negotiations by the end of 2027 if it maintains its current pace of reforms.
  • But North Macedonia, an EU candidate since 2005, remains stalled on the road to accession.
  • That contrast will be particularly evident at Wednesday's EU-Western Balkans summit in Brussels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Union's enlargement drive has regained momentum: Montenegro could become the bloc's 28th member in 2028, while Albania is rapidly advancing through accession talks and could complete accession negotiations by the end of 2027 if it maintains its current pace of reforms.

But North Macedonia, an EU candidate since 2005, remains stalled on the road to accession.

That contrast will be particularly evident at Wednesday's EU-Western Balkans summit in Brussels.

"The Western Balkans' future is in the European Union. Their accession is our priority, our shared ambition and a crucial geopolitical investment in these turbulent times," European Council President Antonio Costa said ahead of the meeting.

North Macedonia formally opened accession talks with the EU in July 2022 but has yet to open the first of the EU's six negotiating clusters, the groups of policy areas through which candidates align their laws and institutions with EU standards.

But the lack of movement does not mean the country is unprepared for membership.

EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said in November that North Macedonia was "among the countries with the highest level of preparedness" in aligning with EU law and had recently accelerated reforms under the EU Growth Plan.

However, she added, "the handbrake on its accession negotiations is still on.".

Kos remarked that to release this handbrake and open the first cluster, North Macedonia must adopt the constitutional amendment agreed with the EU in 2022.

For years, a dispute with Greece over the country's name blocked North Macedonia's progress along the EU accession path.

Although the 2018 Prespa Agreement resolved the dispute, and the country changed its constitutional name, clearing the way for NATO membership, a breakthrough on EU accession did not follow.

Bulgaria later blocked the process amid disputes over history, language and identity. A compromise brokered during the French EU presidency in 2022 lifted the veto but made further progress conditional on North Macedonia amending its constitution to explicitly include Bulgarians among the country's recognized communities.

The amendment requires a two-thirds majority in parliament, which has so far proved unattainable.

From the EU's perspective, this is no longer a Bulgarian veto, but a condition North Macedonia accepted as part of its negotiating framework.

"It [North Macedonia] is not blocked by a member state. It is blocked because it doesn't want to date to do what it knows needs to be done," Gert Jan Koopman, the European Commission's director-general for Neighbourhood and Enlargement Negotiations, recently told an Atlantic Council podcast.

North Macedonia's government sees the problem differently.

EU membership remains its declared strategic goal, but Skopje wants guarantees that amending its constitution will not simply pave the way for further demands from Sofia.

Those concerns are rooted partly in long-running disputes over identity and history: Bulgarian governments have challenged North Macedonia's interpretation of a centuries-old distinct Macedonian identity, while some Bulgarian politicians have gone further, describing Macedonian as a regional variant of Bulgarian, and Macedonians and Bulgarians as one people.

President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova states North Macedonia is ready for talks with Bulgaria and the EU but wants certainty that one constitutional change will not simply be followed by demands for another.

According to recent reports, "We only want certainty. We only want this not to be yet another amendment for the sake of an amendment, followed by another one," she said.

After more than two decades of waiting, the deadlock has also become a domestic political problem in North Macedonia.

Industry observers note that A nationally representative survey by the Institute for Democracy "Societas Civilis" illustrates the contradiction: 71% of respondents support EU membership, but only 24% back the constitutional amendments needed to advance the process. Among ethnic Macedonians, support for the amendments falls to just 11%.

Skopje-based political analyst Petar Arsovski describes the public mood as "passive-aggressive:" Strong support for joining the EU coexists with weak support for making the concession currently required to move forward.

That, he says, helps preserve the status quo.

The dispute is now deeply embedded in domestic politics in both North Macedonia and Bulgaria, where retreat from established positions could easily be portrayed as a national defeat.

The political cost is particularly high in Skopje, where the current government came to power in part on a platform of opposition to constitutional changes under the existing conditions.

For North Macedonia's government, accepting the amendments without further guarantees carries considerable domestic political risks.

The EU, meanwhile, is not offering to reopen the negotiating framework.

According to recent reports, the uncertainty is compounded by debate over how future EU enlargement should work. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have proposed allowing candidates to gradually gain some benefits of membership before formally joining, while stressing that full membership remains the ultimate goal.

According to Arsovski, uncertainty over the future course of enlargement gives ammunition to Eurosceptic narratives and reduces the political incentive for a difficult compromise.

"If these overall conditions remain unchanged, the most likely scenario is that EU summits come and go, while political actors remain dug in, with no real convergence of positions and no genuine commitment to a substantive compromise," Arsovski told DW.

Industry News: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US Army intends to move ahead with detonating five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa despite a ruling to halt it indefinitely, a fresh court filing shows.
  • "To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action," the justice department notified the court on Saturday.
  • The court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation, arguing the army failed to consider safer alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Army intends to move ahead with detonating five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa despite a ruling to halt it indefinitely, a fresh court filing shows.

"To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action," the justice department notified the court on Saturday. "Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.".

The court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation, arguing the army failed to consider safer alternatives.

Industry observers note that the detonation was originally scheduled for Friday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The army now plans to act by 24 November under an emergency exemption.

In the newly introduced filing, the Department of the Army argued that a controlled detonation was necessary to protect the public from an unplanned explosion, a risk it said would become more likely as temperatures were set to fall in the coming days.

"There is an immediate risk that the lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant will explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1C) in the next several days," the filing states.

It argued that the army had removed the doors to the bunker where the barrels were stored in preparation for the detonation and that made the explosives more "vulnerable to temperature changes".

The government has not released details for the rescheduled detonation.

Earlier, the army had warned residents to leave their homes for six hours on the original scheduled day of the explosion, for the duration of the explosion and until the dust settled. An advisory warned "all humans" to avoid being outside in the affected areas while the demolition detonation was set to take place.

Recent findings suggest that lead azide is a highly volatile compound used as a detonator. Earlier this year, the IAAAP found that the material had degraded over time to the point where it was now too risky to move the material, according to Iowa Public Radio.

On Friday, the military said it was working with the Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA to ensure the explosion was done in the safest manner possible.

Military and environmental officials determined that detonating it in place was the safest way to eliminate the explosive safety hazard.

The EPA, which granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the material, said it did so because the explosion risk "presented an imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment".

One of the Environmental groups suing to pause the detonation, the Iowa Environmental Council, argued that many Iowans living within the risk-zone were unaware that the explosion was scheduled to happen.

"There is no safe level of lead exposure, and Iowans were given just days to prepare for the November 20 detonation," the organisation remarked in a press statement.

The Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club, which filed the lawsuit on Thursday that prompted the court-ordered pause, filed a upcoming motion on Sunday in response to the army's filing.

The group asks the court to pause proceedings so that it may submit additional information before the scheduled detonation.

The motion includes declarations from environmental experts and local officials who support pausing the detonation, citing a lack of public notice and questioning the Army's claim that delay would cause significant risks.

US army warns detonation of unstable explosives will create toxic plume.

Tech Report: How to clear the cache on Microsoft Edge

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (343 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has been updating Windows 11 to improve performance on PCs with 8GB of RAM, including by making various apps more efficient and responsive.
  • A quick and easy way to free up some storage space — and a process that many folks stand to benefit from having as part of their regular system maintenance — is to clear the browser cache.
  • Recent findings suggest that the cache is especially useful when you're looking at several pages on a website, since you won't have to re-download elements that are consistent across the domain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has been updating Windows 11 to improve performance on PCs with 8GB of RAM, including by making various apps more efficient and responsive. There are ways for people to boost performance and clean up their system as well, which is particularly key at a time when upgrading a PC's RAM and storage can be debilitatingly expensive.

A quick and easy way to free up some storage space — and a process that many folks stand to benefit from having as part of their regular system maintenance — is to clear the browser cache. This stores certain aspects of websites on your system, such as images, style sheets and scripts. The cache can speed up web browsing and make sites load faster since it recycles parts of webpages that stay the same.

Recent findings suggest that the cache is especially useful when you're looking at several pages on a website, since you won't have to re-download elements that are consistent across the domain. Still, it's good practice to clear out the cache now and again to remove cruft that builds up over time, especially data from sites that you rarely visit.

Sources indicate that if you're a Windows user and you're sticking with that platform's default browser, that means you're accessing the web through Microsoft Edge. Clearing the cache in Edge takes just a few moments of your precious time.

First, you'll have to decide if you want to wipe the cache only on the system you're using or on all synced devices. If it's the former, you'll need to turn off the sync function first. To do that, go to the Settings and more menu in Edge (the button with three dots next to the address bar), then Settings > Profiles > Sync > Turn off sync.

Recent findings suggest that next, you'll want to go to the Clear browsing data page. From the Settings menu, you'll find that by clicking on Privacy, search, and services > Clear browsing data. Next up, click on Choose what to clear.

#138793. Tech Report: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2613 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.
  • You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf.
  • While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Ask Proxy’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website.

It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

In a recent development, unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a latest activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy.

There’s also a work-focused version, which the manufacturer explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.”.

Industry observers note that the personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees.

In a recent development, ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625.

Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone consumers and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

Recent findings suggest that for instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

In a recent development, comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished.

Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies consumers and recommends the next steps.

Sources indicate that it can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.

Comma is free to start and open source.

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized proposal.

The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot currently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future.

The company debuted in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

In a recent development, folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

According to recent reports, one distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Haven distinguishes itself by presenting the concept of a “digital twin” rather than merely serving as a text-based AI assistant.

It has been revealed that according to the company, Haven understands and adapts to your preferences, routines, and decision-making styles, creating a personalized memory graph based on your interactions. As the company describes, “A personal assistant knows what you asked it to do. Haven knows what you would do and how you would do it.”.

Notably, the company envisions future features that customize your experiences across devices, like TV and car.

Presently, Haven is available for free in beta on iPhone and Android devices, and the web. You can also reach Haven by calling or texting (435) 260-6500.

It has been revealed that instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion, valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. People can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company indicates early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions.

The company remains in private beta.

It has been revealed that powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It has been revealed that it can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of users by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Maverick describes itself as an “AI companion who lives in your texts,” acting as a personal assistant that helps manage everyday tasks directly from your messages.

It can fix typos, cancel subscriptions, schedule meetings from voice notes, and help group chats settle on a date for an event. One notable feature is that Maverick asks for your permission before taking action.

The platform also offers hundreds of integrations, including Discord, Gmail, and Slack, allowing it to connect with the apps you already use.

Sources indicate that it’s presently in beta and free to use on iMessage. There’s also a Pro version for €27 per month (or approximately $30.25 USD), which includes 500 tasks a month,  20 connected apps, scheduled tasks, and memory.

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel.

It operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Consumers can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details and flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Customers can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and plans. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

According to recent reports, users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of aims, receipts, dates, files, and other details.

There’s a free strategy available. It works over iMessage, RCS, and Telegram.

Poke rolled out in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities.

Recent findings suggest that poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent company The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Industry observers note that rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is at the moment available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

It has been revealed that instead of waiting for customers to open an app, Skye is an “agentic homescreen” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information.

The company, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet confirmed a public release date.

Stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping consumers come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

It has been revealed that for instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Customers can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and blueprint from scratch.

Szn is designed to coordinate tasks and follow-ups through a single conversation thread. Customers can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.

According to the manufacturer’s website, Szn has served more than 7,500 businesses across 16 countries, completed over 10,000 jobs, and handled 95 hours of calls.

Tab allows users to delegate everyday tasks through familiar messaging platforms. Users can send requests to the assistant via iMessage or WhatsApp, ranging from ordering groceries to finding birthday gifts, and Tab handles the process on their behalf.

The organization emerged from stealth in early October with a valuation of $300 million. Its investors include SV Angel, Valar Ventures, and American Spirit.

The biggest differentiator with Tomo’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations.

Industry observers note that also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Industry observers note that town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms.

In June 2026, the company raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

According to recent reports, underdog is a privacy-focused AI assistant that introduced an invite-only beta in early October 2026. Unlike cloud-based AI services, the model runs entirely on the user’s device, keeping personal data on hardware they already own. The initial release supports Mac and Windows computers, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions planned for the future.

The company intends to offer the app for free initially and has stated that it will never include advertising.

Wajo’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

According to recent reports, A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring owners to hand over their own credentials.

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo claims it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo launched publicly in September 2026 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.

Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.
  • Industry observers note that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it.
  • Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person noted, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

Industry observers note that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person noted, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical upcoming insights to the People’s Republic of China.”.

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have noted.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”.

Sources indicate that gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”.

According to recent reports, the surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

CNN’s Alex Marquardt contributed to this report.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Watch: Democrat who unseated 21-year Republican incumbent notes party needs to 'bring change'.
  • The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.
  • The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: Democrat who unseated 21-year Republican incumbent notes party needs to 'bring change'.

The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

View the 2026 midterm election results.

According to recent reports, sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

In a recent development, hubbard added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District.".

Foxx, meanwhile, mentioned in a statement: "After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I'm humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short.".

Virginia Foxx spent a decade in the North Carolina Senate before representing the state in the House of Representatives.

Hubbard's win, which comes after he lost to Foxx two years ago by nine percentage points, followed a number of Democratic victories in deeply Republican districts including South Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Iowa.

Hubbard, like many Democrats running in the midterms, focused on the rising cost of living in the US during the war with Iran - a top problem for voters.

Trump himself - as well as Vice President JD Vance - have suggested inflation caused by the war in Iran was probably to blame for the Republican losses.

Hubbard has also stated he will also prioritise working families and small businesses, supporting public education and expanding access to affordable healthcare, according to his website.

The remaining House races yet to be called are in Tennessee and Minnesota, while two elections in Louisiana will go to a runoff in December. In Tennessee's fourth district, Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than 300 votes, and in Minnesota's first district, Democrat Jake Johnson is winning by fewer than 500 votes.

Democrats may use their upcoming majority in the House and control of the Senate to investigate conflicts of interest and other actions by the president and those close to him, while the Senate also has the power to confirm or block the president's cabinet and judicial nominations. They will also be able to pass legislation through Congress easily, though Trump still has to give final sign off for it to become law.

However, even with control of both chambers of Congress, they will still have limits on their power as Trump can veto legislation.

Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House.

#138786. 5 underrated Apple Watch shortcuts you can set up in minutes

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1501 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

5 underrated Apple Watch shortcuts you can set up in minutes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your Apple Watch can handle directions, texts, lights and naps with just a little setup.
  • You're stuck outside a bar you'd never heard of until about six hours ago, trying to shout your home address into your wrist for the third time while someone else's Uber pulls up in front of you.
  • The good news is you can still set one up before your next night out, and while you're at it, a few more are worth adding.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your Apple Watch can handle directions, texts, lights and naps with just a little setup.

It's 11PM and raining. You're stuck outside a bar you'd never heard of until about six hours ago, trying to shout your home address into your wrist for the third time while someone else's Uber pulls up in front of you. Your Apple Watch could have had you on your way home with a single tap, if only you'd spent five minutes setting up a shortcut instead of doomscrolling.

The good news is you can still set one up before your next night out, and while you're at it, a few more are worth adding. Your Watch can also text your better half an ETA as you leave work, switch off the lights you always leave on downstairs when you get into bed, put you down for a 20-minute nap without disturbing you and keep its screen dark while you're driving.

In a recent development, shortcuts are made in the Shortcuts app on your iPhone, and they'll only appear on your wrist once you flip the Show on Apple Watch switch in each shortcut's settings. After you've set them up, you can run them from the Shortcuts app, a watch face complication or a Smart Stack widget (or the Action button if you've got an Ultra). If you've got an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, you can also describe what you want in plain English and let Apple Intelligence build a shortcut for you.

According to recent reports, if you're out somewhere unfamiliar, after a night out or a long day at a conference, the last thing you want to be doing is dictating your full address into a tiny screen. Adding a Get Me Home shortcut helps you avoid all this.

Industry observers note that open Shortcuts on your iPhone, tap the plus button and search for the Open Directions action. Tap the destination field, choose Location and pick your saved home address. You can also choose walking, driving or public transit directions and your preferred maps app. To name the shortcut, tap the title at the top of the screen and select Rename, then pick a house icon and a color. Finally, tap the info button, open Details and turn on Show on Apple Watch.

To add this to your watch face, touch and hold the face, tap Edit, swipe across to the complications screen, choose a slot, scroll to Shortcuts and pick the Get Me Home shortcut you just created. A circular slot on a face like Modular works particularly well here. If your route home usually involves a stop like a school pickup, Apple has you covered: iOS 26.4 added multi-stop driving directions to the same action.

"What time will you be back?" is probably the most commonly sent text in any household. Most of the time your phone will ping with it just as you're walking to the car with your hands full. But you can set up a Watch shortcut that works out how long your journey home will take from wherever you are and sends that estimate to the people you choose.

It's quick to set up. Start a new shortcut and search for Get Travel Time in the search bar at the bottom of the screen, then set the destination to your saved home address. Add a Text action and write something like "Leaving now, home in" followed by the Travel Time variable. Add the Send Message action the same way and choose who you'd like it to go to. Since iOS 27, recipients can include groups as well as individual people.

You can make this a single-tap shortcut by switching on Show on Apple Watch and adding it as a complication or a Smart Stack widget. Run it once on your iPhone first, since it will ask permission to use your location and send messages. If you'd prefer not to tap anything, you can instead turn the shortcut into an automation that runs when you leave a saved location, like your workplace. In iOS 27, that trigger lives inside the shortcut and syncs across your other devices.

You're finally home from the bar and your partner's already asleep, but you realize the downstairs lights are still on. Shouting "Hey Siri, turn off the lights!" in the middle of the night isn't exactly ideal, nor is trying to find the Home app on your Watch, which always takes longer than it should when you're pressed for time. A shortcut on your watch face does the job with one (silent) tap.

The easiest way to build this shortcut (if you've got an Apple Home setup) is to set up a scene in the Home app on your iPhone first. Give it a name like "Good Night," then set every light and outlet you want turned off. You can also add the things you want left on, like a hallway light at its lowest brightness or the thermostat at a cooler setting.

It has been revealed that next, create a fresh shortcut in Shortcuts and search the action list for Control Home. Choose the action that runs a scene, then pick Good Night. Turn on Show on Apple Watch and add it to your watch face as a complication like the others.

The same approach works for the morning. A Good Morning scene, for example, could switch on the kitchen lights, turn the thermostat up and boil the kettle if you're British. You can put that shortcut next to Good Night on the same face, which makes it easy to switch between the two. You can also set up an automation on your iPhone that runs when you stop your alarm, which handles the morning half without a single tap.

It's already easy enough to set a timer on your Watch, but setting everything up for a nap usually takes a few steps: start the timer, mute your notifications and then remember to unmute them when you wake up. If you don't mute your notifications, you can bet the group chat will come alive and buzz your wrist within 10 minutes. A simple dedicated nap shortcut can end all that.

According to recent reports, head to Shortcuts on your iPhone, search for the Start Timer action in the bottom search bar and set it to however long you like to nap. Twenty or 25 minutes is a sensible place to start. Then add Set Focus, choose Do Not Disturb and set it to turn off after the same amount of time, so your notifications come back on their own when the timer goes off. Name it Nap, give it a moon icon and switch on Show on Apple Watch.

Recent findings suggest that if you've got an Ultra, you can use the Action button instead. Go to Settings > Action Button on the Watch, choose Shortcut and pick Nap, then press the button to start the nap timer. Otherwise, you can put the shortcut on a complication or in the Smart Stack.

You can apply the same idea to your workouts. Your Watch knows when you start one, and a recent Shortcuts enhancement added the Fitness app to the When I start a workout automation trigger. Pair that trigger with the same Do Not Disturb action and your phone stays silent during a run or gym session.

It's bad enough having modern LED headlights burn out your retinas while driving at night without your wrist also lighting up every time you turn the wheel. Thankfully, you can use Shortcuts to stop that from happening whenever your phone is connected to CarPlay.

In the Shortcuts app on your iPhone, create a new shortcut and add the Set Wake on Wrist Raise action, set to off. To also mute your Watch's sounds (you'll still feel haptic taps), add Set Theater Mode and set it to on. Theater Mode keeps the display dark until you tap it or press a button. Shortcuts may call it Cinema Mode, but it's the same thing.

You'll also need a trigger. Since iOS 27, automations live inside individual shortcuts rather than a separate tab, so add a CarPlay trigger, choose Connects and set it to run immediately so it won't ask for confirmation every time you get in the car. Next, duplicate the shortcut, switch Wake on Wrist Raise to on and Theater Mode to off, and set the trigger to Disconnects so your Watch goes back to normal when you park.

According to recent reports, the same pair of shortcuts will work with your car's regular Bluetooth connection or Driving Focus if you don't have CarPlay. Once your iPhone is talking to the car, you can add an intro to Apple CarPlay using Shortcuts, which runs from the same trigger.

In all, setting up the five shortcuts takes roughly 15 minutes, and each one saves you a few taps every day. The last one can also help cut down on driving distractions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), according to reports in CNN and the Associated Press.

The NCIC is the online database used by federal and local law enforcement to share information about warrants, background checks, and more. The scope of the breach does not yet appear to be clear.

A former FBI official told CNN that they’re not just concerned about “whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.”.

President Donald Trump addressed the reports during an interview Saturday with Fox News, saying, “We just heard about it and I will say that it’s not good.” At the same time, Trump also said that as a result of the breach, “maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise because, you know, you had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax.”.

In September, the FBI reportedly told agents and support staff that their personal information had been stolen in a cyberattack.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam.

South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.

He said he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.

A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools. This prompted officials to act urgently to detect hidden devices, including sending emergency alerts to every single mobile phone in the country.

The Suneung takes up to nine hours to complete, and it plays a massive role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

South Korean high school pupils in Daegu check their answers, a day after the annual college entrance exam.

"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier said 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old said in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

South Korea catches 111 students with newly introduced measures against exam cheating.

South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating.

Breaking: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list.
  • Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery.
  • Recent findings suggest that as I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most.

(Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We’ll give you a heads-up when we get there.).

Recent findings suggest that as I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945.

Knocked unconscious, Kōichi survived and awoke to find his parents and many others were killed in the World War II bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko (Sae Nagatani). But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island. Kōichi saved the day and lived to tell the tale. He reunited with Noriko, who had a strange black bruise on her neck. And we saw a chunk of Godzilla’s remains start to regenerate, leaving things open for a sequel.

According to recent reports, godzilla Minus One was a massive hit, both in Japan—where it remains one of the highest-grossing Japanese films ever—and worldwide, racking up $116 million globally and winning an Oscar for best visual effects. Yamazaki remarked in interviews at the time that there had as yet been no talk of a sequel—while also hinting at future directions a sequel might explore. He later admitted it was a way of planting a seed for what would become Godzilla Minus Zero.

In a recent development, godzilla Minus Zero is set two years after the events of the first film, with Kamiki and Hamabe reprising their roles as Kōichi and Noriko, along with Nagatani as Akiko. The family is just trying to live in peace after the devastation Godzilla inflicted on their country. Alas, a new kaiju emerges, arriving via meteorite and using its tentacles to feed on local wildlife before morphing into a dragon-like creature that causes fresh rampaging destruction. Fans of the genre will recognize this creature as Ghidorah, whose appearance in the film was teased in the various trailers.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t long before Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka)—i.e., the dude with the magnificent wavy gray hair who is director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau—seeks out Kōichi for help in dealing with this upcoming kaiju threat. His team is able to track Ghidorah’s movements via electrical storms and other pertinent weather patterns, thanks to meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa). But the team has no idea how they might defeat this new threat to life and infrastructure. It’s hardly a spoiler to note that at some point, a regenerated Godzilla will come into play.

(WARNING: significant spoilers appear below. Stop reading now if you haven’t seen the film.).

Sources indicate that yamazaki has retained the visual tone that made the film’s predecessor so striking; it feels like classic Godzilla fare of yore, just with 21st century cutting-edge visual effects. If anything, he’s upped his game on the special effects front, reflecting the larger production budget he had to work with. (It’s also the first Japanese movie filmed specifically for IMAX, and it’s well-worth seeing in that format.).

According to recent reports, much of that budget went toward bringing the central monsters to cinematic life, and Godzilla Minus Zero does not disappoint. Ghidorah, for instance, responds to a bombing attack by mutating into its famous three-headed King Ghidorah form, complete with a spiffy fresh superpower: a “gravity beam” that lets the creature levitate entire houses (and, at one point, Godzilla) into the sky before dropping them back to the ground. And the kaiju vs. kaiju battle is spectacular in both scope and execution.

Yamazaki even managed to squeeze in what he called his “bucket-list” special effects shot inspired by a scene in 2008’s Cloverfield: Godzilla looming out of the Atlantic Ocean in front of the Statue of Liberty to wreak havoc on the statue and Newly introduced York City in general. Granted, it occurs in a dream sequence of biologist Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), who survived the Hiroshima blast that killed his wife and children and longs for revenge. And it’s not just indulgence on the director’s part: The scene reinforces the traditional theme of linking Godzilla to nuclear radiation and the horrors of the atomic bomb.

Industry observers note that nor does Yamazaki ignore the human factor via the dilemma of his nuclear family trio. Kōichi must wrestle with his conscience: how can he risk his life again to battle a kaiju when it could mean leaving Akiko an orphan yet again should he fail? Noriko is infected with Godzilla’s radioactive G-cells—the only human to survive the mutations in her own body for so long. But her time could be running out, plus they’ve kept her infection secret for fear she will be taken away by the government for experimentation. Sometimes doing the right thing comes at great personal cost, and watching these quite ordinary people grapple with that reality brings emotional depth to the film.

Sources indicate that the film ends on a suitably bittersweet note, and while Yamazaki hasn’t dropped any hints about a possible third film in the series, we’d love to learn more about Noriko’s strangely symbiotic connection to Godzilla via the G-cells in her bloodstream. Long may he reign.

Godzilla Minus Zero is still playing in theaters.

NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So much for the board not intending to bring him back.
  • NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately.
  • According to recent reports, "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a upcoming industrial revolution," Huang noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for the board not intending to bring him back.

NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately. The board stated in a statement it held a series of meetings and discussions with Huang, who resigned 11 days ago following reports of multiple affairs. It added that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and determined that reinstating Huang posed no risk to national security.

According to recent reports, "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a upcoming industrial revolution," Huang noted. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work.".

According to recent reports, NVIDIA remarked the board members voted unanimously to reappoint Huang, just a few days after Jones said on an earnings call that they did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." In his first public statement since stepping down on November 12, Huang said last week he "would be honored" to return to the helm of the firm he cofounded. He said he'd "seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners and customers" for him step back into the CEO position.

Huang's reinstatement follows two weeks of turmoil at NVIDIA. The board said on November 8 it had opened an investigation into reports that Huang was "the target of a foreign intelligence effort." He admitted to having an affair following reports linking him to Alice Huang, a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese spy. On November 11, The Fresh York Times reported Huang also had an affair with one of his subordinates at NVIDIA. By the following morning, he had departed the tech giant. The board appointed Jones as board chair and Kress — NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President — as interim CEO.

The board met on Sunday night to vote on Huang's reinstatement, according to Semafor, which previously reported that several directors had pushed for him to return. President Donald Trump was among the external figures who wanted Huang to be reappointed. Amid reports that he called into the meeting, Trump confirmed to CNBC he spoke to the board. "And I convinced them," he remarked. "I made the deal." He added that he told Huang to "work hard" in a conversation they had after the meeting.

According to recent reports, "The country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to national security," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the company's compliance with US export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and patriotic duty to protect US national security.".

Last week, CNBC reported that Trump's investment accounts have traded between $27 million and $97.5 million of NVIDIA stock since he returned to office in January 2025, including a sale of between $500,000 and $1 million after he was reportedly briefed on Huang's affair in May. Trump's latest financial disclosure showed that, in September, he bought up to $265,000 worth of NVIDIA stock and sold up to $15,000 worth of his shares in the company. The White House told Reuters that third-party financial institutions manage Trump's portfolio. NVIDIA's share price skyrocketed by around 33 percent after Huang's reinstatement.

NVIDIA's board "believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones mentioned in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer.".

NVIDIA's investigation is ongoing and Huang said he'll fully cooperate. He's also set to testify before Congress on December 1. Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee. NVIDIA General Counsel Tim Teter will do the same the following day. It appears they'll testify behind closed doors, though their remarks will at least be transcribed.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Alice Huang is reportedly under federal investigation over her alleged ties to Chinese companies that are noted to have smuggled in chips from the likes of NVIDIA and Super Micro Computer in the face of US export restrictions. In 2023, she became a director of Singaporean cloud computing company Megaspeed, which is said to have since bought over $4 billion worth of NVIDIA chips and equipment. NVIDIA placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in 2025. Megaspeed said Alice Huang left the company two months later. The US Commerce and Justice departments said last week they'd been investigating Megaspeed over potential export control violations since 2024.

Sources indicate that last week, NVIDIA set up a committee to ensure the organization's compliance with US export controls. It stated on Monday it was recruiting a Chief Compliance Officer as well. NVIDIA added that it will "continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.".

Upgrade, 11:59AM ET: Added Trump's claim that he talked to the board and "made the deal.".

A tale of two Nvidias

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.
  • On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no intends for Huang to return.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no intends for Huang to return.

Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the manufacturer’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.

Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.

According to recent reports, and again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. Kirsten:  Sure, never say never.
