    #138707. Blade Runner 2099 is an inventive twist on a cyberpunk classic

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (887 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 The Verge ↗ Open Full Page

    Blade Runner 2099 is an inventive twist on a cyberpunk classic

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Amazon’s series nails the look and tone, but stretches itself a little too thin in places.
    • Amazon’s series nails the look and tone, but stretches itself a little too thin in places.
    • In an age of streaming highlights designed to appeal to distracted viewers, Blade Runner 2099 can feel like a welcome anachronism.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amazon’s series nails the look and tone, but stretches itself a little too thin in places.

    Amazon’s series nails the look and tone, but stretches itself a little too thin in places.

    In an age of streaming highlights designed to appeal to distracted viewers, Blade Runner 2099 can feel like a welcome anachronism. The Amazon series is slow and methodical, just like the movies it follows, as it delves deep into moral ambiguity. It is very Blade Runner, in that it both feels true to the films but also expands on them in novel ways, showing you sides of this universe that have only been hinted at before. It’s just a little too long for its own good.

    Sources indicate that like the movies, 2099 uses the lens of a detective story to explore a much bigger narrative about what it means to be human. The show takes place 50 years after the last film, and a lot has changed. The Blade Runner series is set in a future where humans have developed artificial life-forms called replicants that are nearly indistinguishable from people aside from a few key traits, like being stronger and having a limited lifespan. This made them ideal for working in harsh environments, but they also became second-class citizens, many of whom were willing to fight for whatever kind of life they could, no matter how short.

    In between the events of 2049 and 2099 there was a war between humans and replicants, which flipped the dynamic: Now the replicants are in charge, with humans cataloged and relegated to manual labor. The titular blade runners, a kind of special detective force, are now replicants hunting down any humans who go against this latest order. This sets up a curious dynamic for the show, which centers on two blade runner partners. Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) is a replicant with only a week left to live, spending her remaining time hunting down her missing ex-partner. Soon she’s joined by Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human fugitive posing as a replicant in a ploy to earn freedom for herself and her sick brother.

    This premise allows the show to explore the universe from a few upcoming angles. For one thing, the ambiguity over the differences between humans and replicants becomes even cloudier with the roles reversed. Despite having longer lives and the benefit of an actual childhood (replicants are grown in a lab and enter the world as full-grown adults), people in this time are mostly emotional husks, forced to become subservient just to survive. That’s the main reason Cora is able to successfully go undercover. Her rough upbringing hardened her emotionally, making her more capable of pretending to be a replicant — a being who does not experience emotions like empathy or embarrassment.

    Sources indicate that as blade running partners, the two are pulled across retrofuturistic Los Angeles with very different goals in mind, but they ultimately intersect as Olwen searches for her partner and Cora searches for freedom. I won’t spoil too much, but there’s a MacGuffin that comes into play that has existential ramifications for replicant and human alike, and both detectives are ultimately pulled into its orbit.

    Exploration of this premise expands the universe of Blade Runner. Some developments are largely implied — you don’t actually see the war, only its aftermath, and there are rumors of a Mexico City that remains a safe haven for humans — but others are shown in exquisite detail. There are parlors where replicants can live out different lives using disturbingly realistic bodysuits, and dingy, underground dance clubs where humans let loose away from replicant eyes. It helps that 2099 looks incredible, evoking the scuffed-up cyberpunk future of the films through chunky computers and intimidatingly brutalist architecture. And yes, both Olwen and Cora wear extremely cool jackets, like all blade runners should.

    According to recent reports, the main issue is that the series feels like it stretches itself too thin at times, particularly during the middle episodes, which can sag with unnecessary storylines and characters that are underdeveloped. This is exacerbated by the slow-burn structure, which works well for a film but can feel a bit much across eight episodes. Potentially fascinating characters, like a delightfully deranged replicant played by Amy Lennox, feel disappointingly flat. 2099 tries to fill up some of its time by being more action-focused compared to the films, but these scenes often feel at odds with the rest of the show. And as much as I love tense sequences, like the Voight-Kampff test where characters stare each other down like gunslingers in a Western waiting for someone to make a wrong move, this happens a few too many times during the show, diluting the scenes’ impact.

    Perhaps the best thing about Blade Runner 2099 is that it ends at all. In an age when franchises are frequently bled dry, 2099 is a relatively brief and welcome dip back into a beloved universe, one with a very final finale. It’s an ending that, much like the original film, opens up all kinds of new questions — ones that may never be answered.

    Blade Runner 2099 starts streaming on Amazon Prime Video on November 25th.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that in a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the tech giant’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S.
    • According to recent reports, the decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker.
    • Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that in a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the tech giant’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.

    According to recent reports, the decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board remarked it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.

    Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.

    In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump mentioned in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.

    Industry observers note that trump also noted the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

    A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.

    The firm said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”.

    Industry observers note that just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the manufacturer’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones remarked they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

    Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones stated the board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners and customers.

    It has been revealed that “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the tech giant,” Jones noted. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”.

    In a statement, Huang stated he was honored to return to his role as the head of the firm he co-founded in 1993.

    It has been revealed that “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

    In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social, saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”.

    The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair.

    It has been revealed that “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.

    According to recent reports, huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement.

    Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence, while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom. Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise customer experience firm Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, remarked on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.

    The newly introduced round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

    Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra noted that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The organization late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.

    That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

    Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

    Industry observers note that startups operating in the CX space have seen multimillion-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI organization ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.

    During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

    • The upgrade swaps blocky wireframes for a photorealistic overhead feed and promises a “25x” safety boost, even as federal regulators continue investigating the software.﻿.
    • Sources indicate that tesla has begun rolling out Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15, calling it a ground-up overhaul of its end-to-end driver assist system.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The update swaps blocky wireframes for a photorealistic overhead feed and promises a “25x” safety boost, even as federal regulators continue investigating the software.﻿.

    The upgrade swaps blocky wireframes for a photorealistic overhead feed and promises a “25x” safety boost, even as federal regulators continue investigating the software.﻿.

    Sources indicate that tesla has begun rolling out Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15, calling it a ground-up overhaul of its end-to-end driver assist system. The centerpiece is Reality View, a real-time generative display that swaps out old wireframe graphics for a live, overhead camera angle that lets drivers see and tap to influence what the car plans to do next.

    Sources indicate that the third-person perspective renders buildings, crosswalks, pedestrians, and surrounding traffic with a photorealism that has drawn immediate comparisons to Grand Theft Auto VI (which conveniently launched just days earlier). Even Elon Musk couldn’t resist the comparison on X, posting “FSD is GTA irl” shortly after the update dropped on Saturday.

    Under the hood, FSD v15 runs on an upgraded vision encoder shared across Tesla’s FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus humanoid robot programs. By training the model on millions of online videos, Tesla claims its AI learned to prevent serious driving mistakes 25 times more often while using less computing power. Of course, the enhancement is built for vehicles running Tesla’s newer AI4 (HW4) hardware and upcoming Cybercab platforms, leaving millions of older HW3-equipped cars behind.

    Beyond the flashy visuals, v15 packs several practical upgrades. A fresh Bike Rack Mode lets drivers engage FSD even with hitch accessories attached (though it disables reversing, Summon, and Autopark). The system can now automatically ease off the speed near traffic cameras, with an option to override and permanently mute specific cameras after two cancellations. Tesla also promises sharper hazard avoidance for potholes, standing water, and small animals, alongside smoother speed handling in school zones and bad weather.

    Meanwhile, navigation learns preferred neighborhood routes and favorite parking spots over time, and the cabin camera can now track driver attention through hats and sunglasses while dialing back nagging alerts at higher speeds. Tesla has a pretty poor reputation for ensuring its drivers stay alert while using FSD, so hopefully this upgrade can improve that.

    Still, Reality View raises an obvious question: is a hyper-detailed, video-game-style feed on the center touchscreen a helpful window into the car’s “brain,” or a tempting fresh distraction? For drivers who find the live feed overwhelming, Tesla includes a map-only option and a stripped-back “quiet mode”.

    Recent findings suggest that tesla’s bold “25x” safety claim also lands amid intense federal scrutiny. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is actively investigating roughly 2.9 million FSD-equipped vehicles over reports of Teslas blowing through red lights, crossing railroad tracks improperly, and driving into oncoming lanes. Alongside dozens of cumulative fatalities linked to Tesla’s driver-assistance systems since 2019, the probe is a stark reminder of the gap between Tesla’s autonomous ambitions and a system that still legally requires a human to keep their eyes on the road.

    #138696. F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1889 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend.
    • Sources indicate that the Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar.
    • But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing.

    Sources indicate that the Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor.

    But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle.

    According to recent reports, and because it takes place at night, in the desert, in November, it’s cold—much, much colder than anywhere else the sport will visit all year. This coming weekend in the Middle East, track temperatures may well exceed 122° F (50° C ); on Saturday night in Nevada the track was a mere 59° F (15° C). Combined with the concrete streets, that spells low grip, but there is an added benefit—virtually no tire wear or overheating.

    And finally, there’s the slipstream. This was far more powerful than in years past, thanks to the newly introduced aerodynamic regulations. We saw this play out in qualifying, which took place on Friday night when Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli snatched pole position by being the last man on track and benefiting from all the cars in front of him each clearing the air out of his way. Conversely, the Ferrari duo of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc had a torrid time by not working together—a preview for the following night, as we’ll see….

    Antonelli’s pole was rapidly forgotten, though, as the latest World Champion would only start 6th thanks to a grid penalty for using an engine component outside his allowance.

    Sources indicate that because of the penalty, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was on pole, with Mercedes’ George Russell next to him. To say there is little love lost between these two drivers would be to undersell the depths of animosity to that relationship. This was evident in FP3, when the pair clashed on track in what looked like a repeat of the Verstappen/Liam Lawson incident in Mexico. This time, no penalties were handed out.

    “He does this week in, week out with many drivers, and everybody accepts it, and I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to that guy,” Russell said on Friday. That set up the prospect of a lap 1, turn 1 coming together, but instead the start of the race was remarkably clean. But not boring.

    Within a lap, Russell had passed Verstappen for the lead on a straight, before the Red Bull reclaimed the position going into turn 17 on the last corner. This set the tone of things to come, with the Mercedes repeatedly getting past the Red Bull at turn 14, only for Verstappen to regain the lead through sheer commitment, taking back his lead in the corners.

    According to recent reports, don’t be tempted to call this yo-yo racing; it was nothing like the races we saw early in the season, when everyone was still trying to understand their hybrid deployment and regeneration strategies. Like an oval race, knowing when to try to move up through the pack was vital; choosing it wrong meant losing multiple positions, not just one. But like an oval, it was also possible to work one’s way up through the pack.

    Industry observers note that the second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar looked more competitive than at any other time this year, and, had the two teammates worked together, they might have been able to leapfrog each other to break free of the pack—a tactic we see used to good effect on oval races. Whether Verstappen’s temperament would allow him to let his teammate past even temporarily remains unknown (I have my doubts), but Red Bull never tried it, instead ordering Hadjar to hold position, leaving him vulnerable to attack from behind. His day was ruined when his front wing exploded on lap 25, dropping him from 3rd to dead last.

    So Verstappen never broke free of the chasing pack, with five or six cars covered by as little as 2.5 seconds for much of the time.

    Again and again Russell took the lead briefly but lost it again to Verstappen, who worried over the radio that the Mercedes team had figured out his strategy and was going to be able to defeat it on the last lap.

    “I think in the beginning we had the deployment immediately correct, but of course, people are learning and watching what you’re doing. At one point, I couldn’t get back into the lead before the start-finish line, so I just—that’s why I asked the question,” Verstappen said after the race. “But I think we had it set up well, and it was just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so significant that you—it was just impossible to drive off, and it was just crazy how many people were just following you.”.

    In a recent development, but Mercedes fumbled. George Russell crashed into a barrier on lap 47—probably as he ran over a piece of Hadjar’s broken wing, preventing him from braking in time. And Antonelli blew his own chance when, instead of charging his battery for that last lap, last corner pass, he accidentally drained it entirely. The team that claimed the 2026 Constructor’s championship last time out in Mexico had to settle for another weekend off the podium.

    Sources indicate that verstappen claimed his 75th win, one he noted was more like Mario Kart than any of the previous 74. McLaren’s Lando Norris was just 0.64 seconds behind him, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri a similar gap behind his teammate. The orange pair worked well together and took home a significant bounty of points in their fight with Ferrari for second place in the constructor’s championship as a result.

    Industry observers note that ferrari’s Friday was already being called a disaster, as the two red cars couldn’t make it into the third and final qualifying session. Had they worked together to tow each other, this might have been possible. But things are far from harmonious at Ferrari between their two very closely matched drivers, with plenty of fireworks recently in Mexico City.

    During the race things got worse. The cars stratified themselves according to performance, which meant teammates running together often. Early on, Hamilton and Leclerc kept it mostly clean, although Hamilton earned a 10-second penalty when he went off track to avoid Norris and Leclerc, dropping him to 14th at the time. With safety cars, strategy, and that strong tow, Hamilton clawed his way back up the running order and was again in front of Leclerc by lap 34.

    Four laps later, Leclerc tried to pass Hamilton—despite being specifically told by his team five corners earlier to hold position. Leclerc misjudged it, like he did in Monza and Mexico, and the cars made contact, dropping Hamilton to 10th. The race stewards clearly apportioned blame to Leclerc, handing him a 10 second penalty. Hamilton eventually finished 7th, Leclerc 10th.

    It has been revealed that leclerc appears desperate to show the team he’s better than the seven-time champion it hired to race alongside him, but time and again his efforts end badly, costing the team points instead. Team boss Fred Vasseur had evidently read Leclerc part one of the riot act before the media pen—the palid, tear-stained face of the Mongasque driver was that of a man who looked like he knew he really screwed up this time. Having signed a massive multiyear contract, his position with the team is presumably safe. But were I Vasseur, one of Ferrari’s reserve drivers would be getting a call to get ready to replace him for the weekend in Qatar.

    Like Leclerc and Hamilton, Russell has been writing checks about Verstappen his racing hasn’t cashed, and in the post-race interview, Verstappen had simply epic levels of disrespect for the other driver.

    It has been revealed that “The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track, and honestly, you know, for me, it doesn’t really bother me because he’s so far below my level that it doesn’t really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know? So it doesn’t bother me,” Verstappen said. “And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening, so I was like, “Fantastic, my day is only getting better.” And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete.”.

    According to recent reports, so many unique circumstances went into making this particular Las Vegas Grand Prix as exciting as it was, and there’s little chance the next two rounds, which both take place in the Middle East, will see similar conditions. But F1 can take something away from this race to make future seasons better, and it’s to do with the tires.

    It all goes back to the 2010 Canadian Grand Prix. Like this year in Vegas, Canada 2010 was chaotic. The weather was cold, the traction zones were covered in a low-grip surface to combat the tarmac disintegration seen the years before, and the action was unpredictable as each team tried to figure out on the fly how best to adapt.

    In a recent development, F1’s powers that be saw this, and when they awarded Pirelli a sole supplier contract for tires the following year, they instructed the tech giant to make race tires that would cause the same effect. Of course, it hasn’t ever worked out like that. Canada 2010 was a one-off and caught the teams off guard. But running the same Pirelli tires race after race, everyone swiftly figured out the optimal strategy, leaving little room for chaos.

    Industry observers note that and the Pirelli tires, while better than they once were, are still difficult to drive on. Pirelli mandates high minimum pressures out of fear of tire failures and next week in Qatar has told teams they cannot run a set for more than 27 laps. And as we frequently see in races, tires that stay within their temperature window while running in clean air can rapidly overheat when following behind another car. In the wake of a car ahead, the following car has less downforce and will slide more in the corners, which puts more heat into the tires, and the trailing car falls behind instead. Pirelli makes the tires that F1 asks for, but after this weekend’s race, it’s time for the sport to ask for something different.

    Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1198 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Australia's Chris Bowen sits at the top table at the summit surrounded by other delegates.
    • Countries have failed to reach a major newly introduced deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
    • Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Australia's Chris Bowen sits at the top table at the summit surrounded by other delegates.

    Countries have failed to reach a major newly introduced deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.

    Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.

    But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

    Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.

    The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.

    UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, remarked he was "deeply disappointed".

    He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he mentioned were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".

    Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

    "That is the reality," he mentioned on Monday.

    After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a latest, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.

    Sources indicate that but the words "fossil fuels" did not appear anywhere in the text. The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023, when countries agreed to "transition away" from fossil fuels in energy systems.

    The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, made it clear that the EU "strongly" objected, saying that the "decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change".

    "It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels," he noted.

    Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31.

    Other countries, such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, also criticised the deal for doing nowhere near enough to tackle the pace of climate change.

    A first draft of the deal on Monday mentioned "fossil fuel" or "fossil fuels" six times, but that was unacceptable to oil-producing nations.

    Saudi Arabia's delegate Mohammad Ayoub noted that Arab countries "continued to engage in good faith" but argued that they only accounted for a small proportion of historical greenhouse gas emissions.

    Russia warned not to "turn to slogans" over coal, oil and gas, claiming that if countries moved away from fossil fuels too quickly it would lead to "fuel poverty".

    Whatâs next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?

    Climate advocates reacted with dismay at the failure of the talks.

    Former US vice-president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was "outrageous that a handful of petro-states have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels".

    The COP process was "in need of significant reform", Gore wrote on X, as most countries sought "to move forward in good faith.".

    "It's time that we empower those leaders with a reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world," he added.

    Another major sticking point has been money for poorer countries to adapt to the impacts of climate change, such as more intense heatwaves and more severe droughts.

    Last year at COP30 in Brazil, nations agreed to triple the finance for that purpose.

    Sources indicate that but this year's deal contained no reference to concrete figures, nor the baseline against which that pledge would be measured. This raised fears it would give richer nations too much wriggle room.

    "Rich nations and polluting governments cannot keep arriving empty-handed," noted Mohamed Adow of Power Shift Africa, an African climate and energy think tank.

    The UK's Energy Secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, described the failure to reach a political agreement as "immensely disappointing".

    "This only strengthens our resolve to work with partners around the world on the genuine progress made in Antalya on tackling the climate crisis," she mentioned, adding that the UK's commitment was "unwavering".

    While talks were hosted in Antalya in Turkey, Australia led the official negotiations - creating what some observers described as a chaotic dynamic.

    Chris Bowen, Australian government minister and COP31 president of negotiations, said there were "unbridgeable red lines" in the discussions.

    He pointed to "the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory". At the same time, "the impacts of climate change are getting worse", he stated, raising the stakes.

    The year 2026 could end as the hottest on record and has brought extreme weather and natural hazards to much of the world, from summer heat and drought in Europe to flash flooding in Nepal.

    And COP31 was the first annual UN conference to formally discuss how one of the key international targets for limiting climate change would be missed.

    In the Paris talks of 2015, nearly 200 countries agreed to try to limit global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels of the late 1800s, aimed at avoiding some of the worst effects of climate change.

    The UN says the Paris deal has driven "near-universal" climate action. In the early 2010s, global warming of 4C or more was thought to be a serious possibility by the end of the century.

    Now, the world is likely to limit warming to about 2.8C by 2100 based on current government policies, the UN indicates.

    But action has not been fast enough to meet that Paris goal, with the world likely to "overshoot" 1.5C of long-term warming in the next few years.

    Many countries say they are committed to eventually bringing warming back down to 1.5C, but that will require an ambitious ramping up of technologies - which do not yet exist at scale - to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

    Although the main deal fell through, some agreements were reached, including progress on a "just transition mechanism" - a framework to support workers and communities as economies shift towards clean energy.

    The COP31 president also said more than 80 countries backed Turkey's target to increase the share of global energy use met by electricity to 35% by 2035.

    But following the weekend's events, some have questioned whether the UN climate process - which relies on consensus - can succeed in a geopolitically divided world.

    The UN's climate chief, Simon Stiell, stated he would seek advice on potential reform to the process, with the next conference scheduled for November 2027, COP32 in Ethiopia.

    "[The consensus process] has worked to get us where we are," he told the BBC. "It got us through Paris... so it can work," but acknowledged it "fell short" on Sunday.

    The UN climate process has "suffered setbacks before and come back stronger," Stiell told delegates. "It must do so again.".

    COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.
    • As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.
    • According to recent reports, for the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.

    As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.

    Many countries were not buying it.

    According to recent reports, for the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis. Countries did adopt several decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels, and a proposal to assess progress on climate adaptation.

    The failure to agree on an overarching conference statement reflected deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much climate financing developed countries should provide to developing nations hit by costly climate disasters.

    The European Union, as well as several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, noted they would not accept the proposed text from the conference leaders.

    Recent findings suggest that cover decisions at the annual conferences usually focus on fresh steps or language that could reinforce international efforts to slow global warming. A central aim at this meeting was to set quantifiable but voluntary global goals for the widespread electrification of economies, and to increase funding from developed countries to help developing countries adapt to climate impacts.

    In 2022, the UN conference in Egypt agreed to establish a loss and damage fund to help vulnerable countries pay for irreversible climate impacts. A year later in Dubai, delegates from more than 190 countries agreed, for the first time, that a “just and orderly” transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems is needed to slow global warming.

    Recent findings suggest that since then, international collaboration on climate problems has declined amid increased conflict, rising oil and gas prices and economic insecurity. The talks in Turkey ran two days beyond the scheduled end without reaching broad agreement on potential next steps, an outcome that won’t kill the global effort but is widely viewed as a serious setback.

    But compromise for the sake of consensus is not enough, said Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, a climate envoy for the Marshall Islands Ministry of the Environment.

    Recent findings suggest that “We will not be forced to accept false solutions,” she remarked. “We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests.” As written, she added, the Antalya Pact undermines her country’s security and threatens its future.

    It has been revealed that “People are dying, seas are rising, and ecosystems are collapsing,” Jetn̄il-Kijiner mentioned. “Are we so divorced from reality that we take backward steps, even as overshoot threatens to overtake us? To accept this deal would be a betrayal to the Marshallese people.”.

    Sources indicate that it’s not the first time Pacific Island nations threatened by rising seas have objected to the outcome at one of the United Nations’ annual conferences. During the 2023 UN talks in Dubai, a final text was adopted even though a delegation representing 39 small island developing states objected because they were still outside the plenary meeting, trying to coordinate their position.

    But in Antalya, the divide ran much deeper. The economically powerful and politically influential European Union, representing 28 member countries, also rejected the proposed agreement.

    Ireland’s climate, energy, and environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, said the European countries formally objected to the cover decision because it fell short of what the global climate crisis demands.

    “We will not endorse a decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the key driver of climate change, and not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels,” remarked O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU during Ireland’s rotating presidency.

    Egypt and Brazil, hosts of the UN climate talks in 2023 and 2025, also criticized the text proposed by COP31 president Kurum of Turkey and Chris Bowen of Australia, president of the conference negotiations.

    Liliam Beatris Chagas de Moura, director for climate at Brazil’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, mentioned she was disappointed that this year’s conference did not sustain the momentum from last year’s talks in her country.

    Sources indicate that mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator with the Saudi Arabian energy ministry, remarked the 22-member League of Arab States supported the proposed Antalya Pact. He criticized developed countries for using up most of the global carbon budget, the amount of fossil fuels that can be burned without overheating the planet, and then asking developing countries to give up the very energy sources that fueled their own growth.

    Ayoub condemned some countries’ opposition to including references to carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture and storage in the pact, calling their resistance to those technologies unscientific.

    Carbon capture and storage are not close to being deployed fast enough “to keep 1.5 degrees within reach,” he mentioned, referring to the long-term goal of limiting the average global temperature increase established by the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

    “We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table, and that countries select from these solutions depending on their national circumstances.”.

    UN Secretary-General António Guterres mentioned he was “deeply disappointed” that the talks ended without consensus on an overarching agreement.

    “But this setback does not change the facts,” he stated. “Fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis. We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it.”.

    Bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species, and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

    This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News.

    Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia’s board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals.
    • The reinstatement, revealed Monday morning, is “effective immediately” and was based in part on “input from senior levels of the United States government” that assured the board members that “Mr.
    • Recent findings suggest that that assurance comes despite Huang’s admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia’s board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals.

    The reinstatement, revealed Monday morning, is “effective immediately” and was based in part on “input from senior levels of the United States government” that assured the board members that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

    Recent findings suggest that that assurance comes despite Huang’s admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures.

    Industry observers note that huang had been seeking a return to Nvidia since shortly after his resignation, reportedly forming a war room to strategize how best to bring it to pass. Last week, Huang posted on social media that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the tech giant, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

    President Trump has also been a major backer of Huang’s return to Nvidia. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” he wrote on Truth Social last week. “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” In a social media post immediately following the reinstatement, Trump called it “the correct and proper decision” and confirmed that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”.

    Appearing on CNBC Monday morning, Trump remarked that he had spoken to the Nvidia board “directly and indirectly” about Huang’s reinstatement, and that Huang “did nothing wrong.” Losing “the brainpower of someone like [Huang]” would be “a much bigger threat” than anything related to his alleged interactions with China, Trump said.

    “We’ve done a very thorough investigation and the investigation demonstrated that… he had bad judgement having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents,” Trump said. “You have to protect our geniuses and there aren’t enough of them.”.

    Industry observers note that huang’s tenure at Nvidia dates back to the firm’s founding in 1993, when he and three cofounders were focused on the then-nascent field of GPU hardware aimed at PC gamers. In the decades since, the highly parallel cores in those GPUs have been embraced first by cryptocurrency miners and then AI companies, propelling the company to its position as the most valuable in the world at its October peak.

    Nvidia stock—the price of which had sunk roughly 25 percent since Huang’s resignation was announced and nearly 50 percent since its peak—was up about 30 percent in early morning trading in the immediate aftermath of Huang’s reinstatement announcement.

    Huang’s return in some ways echoes that of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was fired almost exactly three years ago after the board mentioned it “no longer has confidence in his ability to continue leading OpenAI.” Two weeks later, Altman was back at the helm after many employees threatened a mass revolt and departure if he wasn’t brought back.

    In Huang’s case, the revolt following his departure came not from employees but from fellow titans of the tech industry. Executives including Altman, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI’s Elon Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey are among the prominent industry figures who have publicly offered him support in the days since his resignation.

    In its statement, the Nvidia board reiterated that it has retained independent counsel and formed a committee of independent directors to investigate what it calls Huang’s targeting by “a foreign intelligence effort.” The company has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to “oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” and is seeking to hire a new chief compliance officer position.

    This story has been updated to reflect Trump’s statements to CNBC.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    How Ukraine drone attacks on Russian ships unfolded.

    A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones at a port in Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

    There was an explosion on the warship at the Benghazi naval base in the early morning, while it was docking for fuel and supplies ahead of its return to Russia, local authorities stated.

    Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

    Sources indicate that the local health ministry stated it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast of the port. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

    Following the strikes, the Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declined to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

    Libya's two governments - the UN-recognised government in the capital, Tripoli, and a rival administration in the east - have both condemned the attack.

    The Tripoli foreign ministry said the country would not accept being drawn into the conflict.

    It mentioned foreign forces would not be allowed to use Libyan ports and civilian infrastructure for military purposes.

    The eastern government, based in Benghazi, called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty.

    Seven naval drones were deployed to target and sink the corvette Merkury, one of Russia's newest ships, Zelensky mentioned in a statement on Monday. He added that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed.

    The Ukrainian president noted the second ship was the MV ANGARA, a Russian container carrier.

    The attack came the day after a Russian cargo vessel was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning.

    Finnish defence forces noted Ukraine was likely to be behind the attack. Kyiv has not commented.

    Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that the "expansion of terrorist activity in the Baltic" was a "dangerous trend" and has said "it is, of course, leading to an escalation of tensions in the region.".

    When questioned over the attacks in Libya, Peskov said information would be provided by the country's defence ministry and added: "We paid attention to Zelensky's statements about it".

    Peskov declined to comment on the strikes on Russian ships in Libya and said that that information would be provided by Russia's Defence Ministry.

    The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks on Sunday, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

    "Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external.

    Industry observers note that videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also indicates a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

    Satellite imagery showed a ship on fire at the port.

    US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it mentioned showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.

    Neither of Libya's rival administrations has formally declared support for either side in the Russia-Ukraine war, but they have contrasting ties with Moscow and Kyiv.

    The head of the Libyan National Army, which controls much of the east of the country, has longstanding links with Russia.

    The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) noted the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.

    Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

    It mentioned Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.

    GNS has accused the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU) of hosting Ukrainian military personnel and allowing them to operate from Libyan territory against Russian targets.

    Separately, the GNU warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.

    It noted such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".

    Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.

    Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.

    In March, Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta with "uncrewed sea drones" launched from the Libyan coast.

    As well as having an economic impact on Russia, hampering the ability of their so-called shadow fleet of tankers to export oil and gas, attacks like this are seen as humiliating to the Kremlin, according to Dr Jalel Harchaoui of the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).

    But it is not only Moscow that will want to react to this latest incident. The ship was in the region as part of a deal with the government of eastern Libya - allied with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army.

    According to recent reports, harchaoui noted Haftar will take the attack as a personal slight. "You're going to have a response by the Haftar family. They will ask questions about who is hosting the Ukrainians.".

    Additional reporting by Benedict Garman and Shayan Sardarizadeh, BBC Verify and Basma El Atti.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Turkish security forces and wildlife authorities were searching woods in the north of Istanbul on Monday for an animal believed to be a lion that was reportedly roaming free, the national parks authority said.

    Industry observers note that in an online statement, the parks authority said police officers in the Zekeriyakoy area, north of Istanbul's European side, reported spotting "an animal resembling a lion" on surveillance cameras at around 9 p.m. (18:00 GMT) on Sunday.

    Industry observers note that grainy images published by the Turkish media showed the lioness walking through a grassy area. It was unclear where the animal came from, though some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home. The Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said it launched investigation focused on identifying its owner.

    Istanbul governor's office stated in an online post, the location of the lion has been identified and the efforts to capture it were underway.

    According to park authority, the search is still underway, with specialist veterinarians also involved in the operation to capture the animal.

    Last year, a lion that escaped from a "theme park" near the southern city of Antalya was shot dead after attacking a man. It remains unclear where the Istanbul lion escaped from but it sparked an outrage among activists and advocates.

    Northern Forests Defense, an independent ecology advocacy movement, called for "the individuals who illegally held this lion captive to be identified and brought to justice.".

    "Removing wild animals from their natural habitats and keeping them in captivity in villas is a crime," it stated on X.

    Wildlife conservationist Gokce Coskun said on X that "there are thousands of people keeping lions illegally in Turkey" and "licensed 'lion parks' have sprung up everywhere.".

    Doganay Tolunay, an ecology professor at Istanbul University, said questions must be raised about how a globally threatened species was brought into Turkey, how it passed through customs and why those keeping it have not been identified.

    Although keeping wild animals as pets are forbidden in Turkey, it has become a hub for the illegal trade in wild animals as traffickers exploit its air links to Africa and Asia.

    In December 2024, a young gorilla was rescued after being discovered at Istanbul Airport on a flight from Nigeria to Thailand.

    Latest Update: Marvel crams every superhero ever into Avengers: Doomsday final trailer

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rumors have been swirling for days that we’d be getting a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, the penultimate film in the MCU’s Phase Six, heralding the end of the so-called “Multiverse Saga.” The rumors were true: Marvel just released the trailer, featuring pretty much every superhero ever represented in the MCU. And it looks like the Avengers will face consequences for messing with the timeline to reverse the blip in End Game.

    It has been revealed that as previously reported, the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts*. Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and Newly introduced Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men.

    Cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the fresh Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. And, of course, Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom.

    We also have the Thunderbolts* (aka Newly introduced Avengers): John Walker/US Agent (Wyatt Russell), Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bob/Sentry (Lewis Pullman), Red Guardian (David Harbour), and Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen). And the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach), and Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn). We’ll also see Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Beast (Kelsey Grammer), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming), and Cyclops (James Marsden).

    For good measure, Marvel threw in Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Xu Shang-Chi (Simu Liu). There will be plenty of cameos, like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), revealed in one of four sneak teasers last year. We can also expect to see (at least briefly) Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Thor’s adopted daughter, Love (India Rose Hemsworth), and Scott Lang’s daughter, Cassie (Kathryn Newton).

    The first trailer dropped in July, just before San Diego Comic-Con, and really just consisted of a heck of a lot of cameos, as the superheroes from the three universes met each other over an ominous voiceover by Thor, warning of an unprecedented threat. It ended with the return of Steve Rogers—and guess what, he’s still worthy of Thor’s hammer, Mjölnir. The following month, Marvel dropped another trailer during its D23 fan event, hinting at Doctor Doom’s tragic backstory.

    Industry observers note that rogers features prominently in the latest trailer, which opens with him and Peggy discussing how they made the right choice, but Steve still feels bad about hiding this truth from their son, who is now a young teen. We knew he had opted to stay in the past and build a life with Peggy at the end of End Game; what we didn’t know is that they did this in the same alternate universe as the Fantastic Four, who show up to recruit him to the latest cause.

    “Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right,” Rogers continues in a voiceover. “But we didn’t know those choices would have consequences.” Whatever the roots of Doom’s grudge against the Avengers, he believes “all of you have lived stolen lives,” adding an ominous: “But now you must give them back.”.

    In a recent development, the rest is largely footage we’ve seen before, with Thor admitting, “I don’t even know who half of you are” to the assembled superheroes, before making his call for them to “stand together” against Doom. Among the new footage is Marsden’s Cyclops facing off against Doom and several Sentinels: He calls, “To me, my X-Men,” except it’s everyone who responds. We also see Steve and Thor bantering about how Steve wielding Mjölnir bothers the Norse god more than he cares to admit. There’s no sign of Wanda Maximoff/The Scarlet Witch, whom Doom revived in a post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest. She might be among the trio of Latverian witches that briefly appear in the trailer.

    Verdict: We don’t know if Doomsday will measure up to Infinity War and End Game, but it’s bound to provide a spectacle.

    Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18, 2026. It will battle it out against Dune: Part III, which also drops that same day. Avengers: Secret Wars is right now slated for release on December 17, 2027, and will mark the conclusion of the MCU’s Phase Six.

    Watch: Nvidia's stock skyrockets after Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO.

    President Donald Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board of directors and "convinced" them to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

    In a brief interview with CNBC, Trump remarked that he gave the board "assurances" that Huang's extramarital affair did not present a national security glitch for the US.

    Huang resigned from Nvidia on 12 November following reports of a series of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.

    The US president, however, has repeatedly expressed support for the embattled CEO despite the vocal opposition of lawmakers - including some Republicans - to his being reinstated at the company.

    The US president has repeatedly downplayed concerns that Huang's affair posed a national security threat.

    It has been revealed that "I spoke to them [the board], let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC. "And I convinced them.".

    Additionally, Trump praised the Nvidia board for acting "really responsibly" in reinstating Huang.

    "They did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know. And we know a lot.".

    "People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him," the president added.

    According to Trump, he spoke to Huang on Sunday night prior to the tech giant's announcement about his reinstatement on Monday.

    Nvidia shares soar after Jensen Huang returns as CEO following affair with alleged spy.

    The president was also asked whether Nvidia stock losses after he resigned last week had influenced his decision to personally intervene.

    Sources indicate that "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term," Trump responded. "He's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about.".

    Before the reinstatement, Trump had repeatedly expressed support for Huang and sought to downplay concerns that a woman he is alleged to have had an affair with, Alice Huang, is tied to Chinese intelligence.

    "I like him," Trump told reporters at the White House last week. "I think he learned a significant lesson.".

    "There is a big group of people that would like him to return," he later remarked.

    The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang.

    How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

    The president's vocal backing of Huang comes despite the concerns of US lawmakers, including some Republicans, over the affair and Nvidia's compliance with US export controls.

    The US president is also personally invested in the company, with recent financial disclosures showing he purchased $265,000 in Nvidia stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of stock in September.

    "Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang," Republican Congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska said on Monday.

    "We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible.".

    Democrats, who will control both chambers of Congress from January, have already expressed a desire to launch investigations into Nvidia and the administration's handling of the firm.

    Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren - who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee - mentioned in a statement that the reinstatement was "reckless".

    "Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," she said.

    • Sources indicate that the United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031.
    • According to recent reports, after FIFA announced its revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup that finished just last summer was around $15 billionn (€13.7 billion), it is clear that US Soccer feels empowered that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.

    Sources indicate that the United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031. It will be the first tournament to feature 48 teams — as is the case with the men. The US has hosted the tournamnent twice before, in 2003 and 1999, and is also the most successful country in its history, having won it four times.

    According to recent reports, after FIFA announced its revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup that finished just last summer was around $15 billionn (€13.7 billion), it is clear that US Soccer feels empowered that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward. With the women's domestic league (NWSL) considered the strongest in the world and the US national team so strong, it is clear that securing the tournament in 2031 is a further sign of the US' committment to women's football.

    "We expect and strategy for the 2031 Women’s World Cup to be the largest women’s sporting event in history," Emily Cosler, US Soccer’s vice-president of strategy told The Guardian.

    Recent findings suggest that the 2035 tournament was also awarded to the sole bidders, England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales. This sees the World Cup return to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966, the only time England's men's team won the competition. The women lost the 2023 final to Spain. It also means that the UK will host two major tournaments in relatively quick succession, with the men's 2028 European Championships also set to be held in England, Scotland and Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

    British Prime Minister Andy Burnham remarked the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.".

    In a recent development, given that FIFA President Gianni Infantino had revealed last year that both bids were unchallenged, this news comes as little surprise. Nevertheless, with the hosts now official, a 48-team tournament marks a remarkable growth for the women's game. For reference, the 2011 World Cup in Germany had just 16 teams.

    Sources indicate that the next World Cup will be in Brazil next year. Eighteen of the 32 teams have already secured qualification, including Germany, for the tournament, which runs from June 24 to July 25.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the organization’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”.

    Sources indicate that the Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.

    Industry observers note that in his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.

    There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he remarked of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”.

    Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.

    Trump stated last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”.

    Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.

    Sources indicate that the NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Organization, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP.

    The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.

    The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, said that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”.

    Sources indicate that critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when consumers are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.

    The Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.

    The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.
